newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Hekmatyar joins anti-Taleban Afghan alliance.
newsitem.headline: Hekmatyar joins anti-Taleban Afghan alliance.

text.p: Afghan faction leader Gulbuddin Hekmatyar agreed on Wednesday to join an alliance opposed to the radical Islamic Taleban militia, Afghan sources said.

Hekmatyar decided to join the alliance formed by ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani and northern militia leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum at a meeting in the northern city of Mazar-i-Sharif, sources close to Dostum said.

Hekmatyar, leader of the Hezb-i-Islami faction, was prime minister in Rabbani's government when the Taleban drove it out of Kabul on September 27. He retains his post in the ousted government under the agreement struck on Wednesday.
Hekmatyar, who fled to the north after the fall of Kabul, stayed out of an anti-Taleban alliance that was formed between Dostum and Rabbani's military commander Ahmad Shah Masood.
Afghan sources quoted by the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press agency said Hekmatyar or his associates had conducted talks with the Taleban in recent weeks with no result.

Under Wednesday's accord, Dostum is to become vice-president in Rabbani's ousted government and will have the right to nominate the defence, foreign affairs and four other ministers. He will also be the military commander in northern Afghanistan.
The sources said Rabbani was expected to come to Mazar-i-Sharif and formally announce the agreement.

The Taleban, who control at least two-thirds of Afghanistan, say Rabbani's government no longer exists and have demanded international recognition for their administration, which aims to spread strict Islamic sharia law throughout the country.
